title: Hierarchical claim graph for tenant-scoped entitlements
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and deliver a tenant-aware hierarchical claim graph that represents entitlements as first-class claims. This ticket covers the role-to-claim transformation, permission evaluation semantics, SSO/SAML group mapping, audit-event wiring for every authorization decision, and admin controls (breakglass, just-in-time elevation and delegations).
background: Current RBAC is a flat role-assignment system that creates scaling issues for multi-tenant resource hierarchies and makes audit trails hard to correlate with resource paths. We need a flexible model where permissions are derived from composable claims attached to principals and resources, enabling efficient evaluation, clear audit provenance, and easier mappings from SSO groups.
design_decisions: Represent entitlements as claims: <subject, claim_type, target_resource_path, attributes> — provides explicit provenance for each permission.
Use hierarchical resource paths (e.g., /org/{org_id}/proj/{proj_id}/dataset/{dataset_id}) and allow claims to target prefixes for inheritance semantics.
Evaluation engine will resolve claims into effective permissions using ordered layers: explicit deny -> direct grants -> inherited grants -> delegated grants; explicit deny takes precedence.
Permission tuple for checks: action, resource_path, principal_id, request_scope, session_tags (e.g., ip, mfa), justification_id (for elevation).
Map SSO/SAML Groups to role templates during sync; templates expand to canonical claims stored in the claim graph (avoid runtime expansion of SSO groups on every check).
Audit events: emit structured events for RBAC_CHECK, RBAC_RESOLVE, ELEVATION_REQUEST, ELEVATION_APPROVAL, and BREAKGLASS_USE; include claim_ids and resolution_trace for repro.
Store claims and resolution traces in tenant-scoped namespaces to simplify deletion/migration and comply with data residency rules.
Introduce short-lived elevation tokens (max 1 hour) issued after approval; all elevation flows must be logged with justification and approver identity.
Cache evaluation results at edge with tag-based invalidation (claim_id, resource_version) to meet latency SLOs while ensuring correctness.
Expose a read-only policy explorer API (dry-run) for customers and SRE to simulate changes and view potential effective grants before enforcement.
Design for eventual offline migration from existing role assignments via a deterministic translator and a dry-run mode that writes RBAC_CHECK logs but does not enforce.
Retention: authorization audit logs kept 12 months by default with an enterprise option for longer retention; sensitive fields redacted per tenant settings.
tradeoffs: Flexibility vs complexity: claim graph enables fine-grained expressiveness at the cost of additional model and UI complexity for admins.
Performance vs correctness: caching reduces latency but requires conservative invalidation semantics and potential stale-deny windows; prioritize deny correctness over cached grants.
Migration effort: automatic translation tools reduce friction but cannot perfectly map all custom role semantics; we accept a manual review phase for complex tenants.
SSO sync semantics: mapping nested SSO groups to claims at sync time improves check-time performance but increases sync complexity and storage footprint.
acceptance_criteria: Auth check API returns decision and resolution_trace; median latency < 10ms for cached checks and < 50ms cold path under P95 load profile.
Every authorization decision emits a structured audit event with claim_ids and tenant_id; events land in the audit pipeline and are queryable in Console.
SSO group -> claim mapping supports nested groups and group-to-template mapping; tests cover Azure AD and Okta sample payloads.
Provide a migration translator that can run in dry-run and produce a report of unmapped items; customers can opt-in to enforcement per tenant.
Breakglass emergency admin path implemented with time-limited tokens and recorded justification; usage alerts wired to oncall Slack and security channel.
Security review completed and documented with mitigations for privilege escalation paths and replay protections.
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: Schema design and API contract for claim graph, resource path encoding, and resolution_trace format.
Week 3: Implement claim storage APIs (tenant namespace, indices) and SSO sync worker prototype.
Week 4: Build evaluation engine with deny-first resolution and unit tests for common inheritance patterns.
Week 5: Integrate audit event emitter and ensure events flow to the audit pipeline with sample dashboards.
Week 6: Implement elevation flows (request/approve/token) and breakglass token generator with TTL and audit tags.
Week 7: Performance tuning (edge cache, invalidation), add metrics, and create Console policy explorer UI mock endpoints.
Week 8: Migration translator tool, dry-run mode for a pilot tenant, and runbook for rollback.
Week 9: Security review, stakeholder demos, and signoff for staged enforcement rollout.
migration_strategy: Phase 0 (Design): Define deterministic translation rules and unmapped heuristics; validate with two pilot tenants.
Phase 1 (Dry-run): Run translation for pilot tenants, emit RBAC_CHECK logs for both old and new models for 2 weeks to compare effects; no enforcement change.
Phase 2 (Opt-in enforcement): Offer tenant toggle to enforce claim-graph decisions; continue monitoring for 30 days and support rollback.
Phase 3 (Default enforcement): Move remaining tenants after migration window; provide guided support and add automated fixes for common unmapped patterns.
Rollback: Maintain legacy role resolver as a fallback route and implement a fast switch in the routing layer to revert enforcement if critical issues are detected.
testing_plan: Unit tests for claim normalization, inheritance and explicit deny semantics.
Integration tests with SSO/SAML assertions (Okta, Azure AD) including nested groups and role-to-claim templates.
Load tests for evaluation engine simulating 10k rps across mixed cache-hit ratios and verifying latency SLOs.
Chaos injection tests validating cache invalidation and resolution correctness after claim changes.
Auditing tests asserting every decision emits the correct structured event and that the console can query them.
rollout_notes: Start with internal tenants and a single pilot customer with simple org hierarchy.
Monitor RBAC_CHECK delta between old and new model on staging and pilot; maintain detailed dashboards for false-grants and false-denies.
Notify customers of migration windows and provide CLI tool for translation preview and manual adjustments.
On-call escalation: product-security -> infra -> authorizations team with a dedicated hotline during tenant cutovers.
